It is located in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The three enshrined deities are as follows{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.
* {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|it|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ko|다카미무스비|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Kami}} (たかみむすびのかみ) - principal deity.
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}} (いちきしまひめのみこと)
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}

In the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, the deity is listed as one seat. It is inferred that originally it enshrined the local land deity "Takamahiko"{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

The name "Takama" in the shrine/deity name is also a local place name. Since old times there has been a theory identifying this area with the legendary {{ill|Takamagahara|ar|تاكاماغاهارا|ca|Takamagahara|de|Takamanohara|eo|Takamagahara|es|Takamagahara|fa|تاکاماگاهارا|fr|Takama-ga-hara|id|Takamagahara|it|Takamagahara (mitologia)|ja|高天原|ko|타카마가하라|min|Takamagahara|ms|Takama-ga-hara|pl|Takamagahara|pt|Takaamahara|ro|Takamagahara|ru|Такамагахара|simple|Takamagahara|sr|Такамагахара|tr|Takamagahara|uk|Такамаґахара|vi|Takama-ga-hara|zh|高天原|qid=Q1141974}}. Other theories say the name derives from a phonetic change of Takamimusubi's name, or that Takamimusubi had an alternate name "Takamahiko-no-Kami," or that "Takama" means "high flatland" on the mid-slope of Mt. Kongō{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}. In the {{ill|Man'yōshū|ar|مان يوشو|az|Manyoşu|be|Ман’ёсю|ca|Man'yōshū|ckb|مان یۆشوو|cs|Manjóšú|de|Man’yōshū|eo|Man'joŝu|es|Man'yōshū|fa|مان‌یوشو|fi|Man’yōshū|fr|Man'yōshū|hi|मानयोशू|hr|Man'yōshū|hu|Manjósú|id|Manyōshū|it|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|ko|만엽집|la|Man'yōshū|mr|मान्योशू|nl|Man'yōshū|pl|Man’yōshū|pt|Man'yōshū|ru|Манъёсю|sh|Man'yōshū|simple|Man'yōshū|sk|Manjóšú|sv|Manyoshu|tl|Man'yōshū|tr|Man'yōshū|uk|Манйосю|uz|Manyoshyu|vi|Vạn diệp tập|wuu|萬葉集|zh|萬葉集|zh_classical|萬葉集|zh_min_nan|Bān-ia̍p-chi̍p|zh_yue|萬葉集|qid=Q834321}}, a well-known poem refers to "Takama of Katsuragi" (Book 7, poem 1337){{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. In the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, Takama Kishino Shrine and Takamayama Satao Shrine are listed in Uchi District and are both identified with shrines on Mt. Kongō's mid-slope in {{ill|Gojō, Nara|ar|غوجو (نارا)|azb|قوجو، نارا|ca|Gojō|ce|Годзё|ceb|Gojō-shi|de|Gojō (Nara)|eo|Goĝo|es|Gojō (Nara)|fa|گوجو، نارا|fi|Gojō|fr|Gojō|gl|Gojō|id|Gojō, Nara|it|Gojō (Nara)|ja|五條市|ko|고조시|mzn|گوجو، نارا|nl|Gojo (stad)|pl|Gojō|pt|Gojō|ro|Gojō|ru|Годзё|sv|Gojō|tg|Гоҷо|th|โกโจ|tl|Gojō, Nara|tr|Gojō|tt|Годзё|uk|Ґодзьо (Нара)|ur|جوجو، نارا|vi|Gojō, Nara|war|Gojō, Nara|zh|五條市|zh_classical|五條市|zh_min_nan|Gozyô-chhī|zh_yue|五條|qid=Q602571}}, which has led to a theory that "Takamahiko-no-Kami" itself is the mountain spirit of Mt. Kongō{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

== History ==
== Overview ==
[[File:Takamahiko-jinja Shirakumo-dake.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Shirakumo-dake ({{ill|Sacred mountains|ar|جبال مقدسة|ca|Muntanyes sagrades|de|Heiliger Berg|es|Montaña sagrada|fa|کوه‌های مقدس|fi|Pyhä vuori|fr|Montagne sacrée|id|Gunung keramat|ja|神体山|lt|Alkakalnis|lv|Svētie kalni|pl|Święte góry|ru|Священная гора|sq|Malet e shenjta|uk|Священна гора|vi|Núi thiêng|qid=Q1595289}})}}{{small|Takamahiko Shrine precinct at lower left.}}]]
Foundation is unknown. The shrine stands on the east foot of {{ill|Mount Kongō|arz|جبل مونت كونجو|ca|Mont Kongō|ceb|Kongō San|cs|Kongó|et|Kongō|fa|کوه کونگو|fr|Mont Kongō|id|Gunung Kongō|ja|金剛山 (金剛山地)|jv|Gunung Kongō|ko|곤고산|lld|Mont Kongō|my|ခွန်ဂိုးတောင်|pl|Kongō (góra)|th|เขาคงโง|vi|Núi Kongō|zh|金剛山 (金剛山地)|qid=Q1348310|lt=Mt. Kongō}} and is said originally to have worshipped Shirakumo-dake (also Shirakumo peak, elevation 985 m) behind the shrine buildings as the sacred mountain<ref name="board">Explanatory board in precincts.</ref>{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

Subsequent history is unclear. Because Takama is a trailhead to Mt. Kongō, it is said that literati and haiku poets visited along with the growth of Katsuragi Shugendō, and the shrine was also called "Hikosawa Gongen"{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1982}}. On the east side of the shrine there was also Takama-dera, a {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}}{{Sfn|Takamahiko Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.
